abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) studies increasingly encompass diverse tissues, donors, disease contexts, and sequencing platforms, resulting in large-scale datasets characterized by substantial technical heterogeneity and inconsistent cell-type annotations. These datasets offer unprecedented opportunities to resolve fine-grained cellular diversity and identify tissue-specific, developmental, and disease-associated cell states. However, existing integration and annotation approaches often struggle to preserve rare or transcriptionally subtle subpopulations, depend heavily on extensively labelled reference datasets or predefined cell-type taxonomies, and can generate latent representations that obscure biologically meaningful lineage relationships and fine-scale cellular structure. We present scRefine, an annotation-aware contrastive learning framework for integrating heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq datasets while refining cell identities from partially labelled data. scRefine learns a biologically structured latent space, enabling improved resolution of rare and transcriptionally similar populations. In particular, scRefine better separates rare or biologically distinct populations that exhibit convergent or overlapping translational states than other integration methods. For example, scRefine cleanly separates SPP1+ melanocytic tumor cells from SPP1+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), indicating that it preserves lineage-specific biological identity despite shared tumor-associated programs. Beyond cell-state resolution, scRefine also preserves continuous biological structure, as demonstrated by its ability to recapitulate the developmental trajectory of the frontal brain in a manner consistent with the patterns reported in the original study. scRefine also calculates a confidence score by estimating cluster membership using nearest neighbour computations for each cell, which aids in defining cells with ambiguous or mixed transcriptional signatures. Across multi-tissue immune atlases spanning 92 fine-grained classes, scRefine consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, rare population recovery, and generalization to unseen datasets. scRefine also maintains high annotation fidelity even when trained with only 1 to 5% labelled cells, greatly reducing the training effort and increasing the generalizability. scRefine is available as an open-source package and offers a robust foundation for constructing coherent, high resolution cell-type reference atlases across studies and technologies.
